questions.text: What is the purpose of a class in JavaScript?
distractors: To define only properties, not methods.
questions.answer: To create reusable blueprints for objects.

questions.text: How do you define a class in JavaScript?
Which method is used in a class to initialize properties?
What does `this` represent inside a class constructor?
Which of the following describes how `this` behaves in an arrow function inside a class method?
distractors: It inherits the value of `this` from the nearest function in a different scope.
It refers to a newly created instance of the class.
It inherits the value of `this` from the global object in strict mode.
questions.answer: It inherits the value of `this` from the enclosing scope where it is defined.

questions.text: What is the primary purpose of the `extends` keyword?
distractors: To define static methods in a parent class constructor.
To create a method in a class.
To initialize default properties in the parent class.
questions.answer: To create a subclass that inherits from a parent class.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of how to create a `Car` class that inherits from a `Vehicle` class?
What is the function of the `super` keyword in a subclass?
distractors: To define a new instance of the parent class.
To delete methods and properties from the parent class.
To access only the static methods of the parent class.
questions.answer: To call the constructor or methods of the parent class.

questions.text: Which of the following describes a static method?
distractors: A method that is inaccessible inside the class itself.
A method that is used only in arrow functions.
A method that is unique to each instance of a class.
questions.answer: A method that belongs to the class itself, not to any instance.

questions.text: How would you access a static property in JavaScript class?
distractors: By using `instance.propertyName` after creating an instance.

questions.text: In which scenario would you use a static method over an instance method?
distractors: When you need to access and modify the instance's properties.
When the method needs to be called on an object instance.
When the method doesn't rely on instance-specific data and operates on class-level data.
questions.answer: When the method operates on data that is shared by all instances of the class.

questions.text: What keyword is used to inherit properties and methods from another class?
Which of the following best describes inheritance?
distractors: It allows a method to return a new object.
It allows an instance to define its own properties.
It allows a static property to be converted into a non-static property.
questions.answer: It allows a class to acquire properties and methods from another class.

questions.text: What happens if a constructor is not defined in a subclass?
distractors: The subclass will inherit the constructor from any class in the code.
The subclass cannot create new instances.
questions.answer: The superclass's constructor will be used by default.

questions.text: What is the primary use of static properties?
distractors: To define default properties for each class instance.
To override methods in a subclass.
questions.answer: To store class-wide data shared across instances.
